I've farmed this land in Quzhou my whole life. I know this ground — the soil is heavy alluvial loam, decent for grain. The Hai River basin has good base fertility but we've been mining groundwater for decades and I feel the guilt of that every time I pump. My children are in Shijiazhuang now. It's just me and my husband, and we hire day labor at harvest.

My land is 15 mu under contract. I will grow the same rotation I've grown for thirty years: **winter wheat** followed by **summer maize** on the same plots. I won't experiment with cotton or vegetables — the market is unpredictable and my back isn't what it was. Grain I understand. The prices are supported by the government and the storage cooperative buys without hassle.

For wheat I'll use Jimai 22, which the county extension station has been pushing and which I've seen yield well on my neighbor's land the past two seasons. I'll reduce irrigation to two times this year — jointing and heading only — because the township water bureau is tracking pump use now and the aquifer is genuinely in trouble. I've attended the water-saving training. Two irrigations is enough if I hit the timing right.

For maize I'll use Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed, as I have for eight years. I'll direct-seed into the wheat stubble with no tillage to save moisture and labor. Summer rain usually covers most of the water need, so I'll plan one supplemental irrigation at silking, but skip it if July is wet.

I'll apply fertilizer at county-recommended rates — I've stopped over-applying since the soil test three years ago showed phosphorus was already surplus.
